Local Design Lab · decision gate · Billing & Health

Two decisions, both with evidence

Billing's third zone was rendered both ways rather than assumed. Health's alarm treatment is gone without losing recognition. And the health data model was re-audited against the schema — which disproved something I told you last pass.

Billing A 294 · B 273Health 379 → 368 Panel 2126 → 2095typecheck rc=0

Billing A/B recommendation: B rendered from one evidence object

Recommend B — Current Bill | Past Due | Payment. The card's third question is how is this being paid, not what happened.

Side by side, A's ledger mostly restates zone one: Tuition $1,850 and Registration fee $75 appear in both zones. Its only unique content is the last payment and a late fee — which is exactly what B's one-line history footer carries. B also puts the actionable fact in a zone: “Autopay paused · Jordan's Visa declined Aug 16” is what an operator needs to resolve the past-due state, and in A it is one buried line. B is also shorter — 273 against 294 — while carrying payer identity, method, split, autopay and history.

The cost, named

Half of B's zone has no owner today. Autopay state and next scheduled charge have no table and no column — only a string in focusPanelConceptCatalog. customer_payment_methods is scoped to the household, not to a payer, so “Jordan · Visa 4242” cannot be built. Responsibility split has no field: billing_responsibility is a composition group with defaultFieldKeys: []. A's zone, by contrast, is fully owned by ledger_transactions (occurred_at · type · direction · amount_cents · customer_id).

So the recommendation is the composition, not the build order: B is the right card, and it is blocked on three small financial gaps. If you want something shippable this quarter, A is buildable today with zero new truth.

Health & Safety calmer 507 × 368 · was 379

The red wash is gone. Normal card surface, a 2px ember rail, a risk glyph beside a small CRITICAL label, the allergen name in ordinary card ink, and red spent on exactly two things: the severity pill and the care instruction. The card carries durable safety information, not an active incident — and it now reads that way.

Hierarchy, condition-linked medication, compact Enrollment health and the emergency footer are unchanged.

Specimens hold at 253 · 368 · 497. The complex child's two critical facts still share one region and still read as recognition rather than alarm.

Health data — verified inventory

Exactly two of eighteen system fields are health, and both bind to entity_type: "enrollment": allergy_notes (textarea) and medication_flag (checkbox). customer_members has no health column at all.

The registry already uses entity_type: "child" for three other fields, and sharedValuesToFieldIds documents the canonical key example as customer_member:allergies. The intended grain is the child; the shipped binding is the enrollment.

Correction to what I told you last pass

I reported that document evidence exists only as form_submission_documents and that a document required outside a form has no owner. That was wrong. I quoted the code comment in REQUIREMENT_KIND_UNSUPPORTED_REASON_V1 instead of checking the schema. public.documents is free-standing, polymorphic (entity_type/entity_id), versioned and checksummed, and already carries the extraction columns; document_field_definitions is a per-org, per-doc_type configurable schema with AI extraction hints. Gap C1 is withdrawn, and D1 shrinks from “build a document owner” to “add a doc_type catalog and a satisfaction evaluator”.

Ownership matrix

CategoryRecommended ownerExists?
ASimple child facts — dietary, accommodation, physician, notesfield_definitions + field_values at customer_memberSubstrate ✅ · binding ❌
BStructured records — allergy, condition, medicationA child-scoped health-fact entity + a registered collection providerSeam ✅ · entity ❌
CDocuments — immunization, physical, authorization, care plandocuments at entity_type: customer_member✅ sufficient
DRequirementsstageRequirementsV1 on the pinned revisionArchitecture ✅ · document kind ❌
ERelationships — emergency contactsperson.contact_role.emergency_contacts✅ project, never own

Why B needs records, not repeaters. An allergy is not a value; it is a record with a lifecycle. It needs identity so a medication can reference it, effective dates so a resolved condition stops appearing, and an evidence pointer so the card can say where the fact came from. field_values has no ordinal and no per-item identity — the alternative is a value_json array in which no item can be referenced, superseded, or traced.

One entity, not three, with a fact_kind discriminator: the card, the requirement evaluator and the packet planner all want one list, and three near-identical tables would triple the resolver, provider and proposal-adapter surface. It stays industry-transferable because the entity is “a structured health fact about a person”, polymorphic by entity_type/entity_id exactly as documents already is.

Gap register — order A1 → D1 → B1

#GapSmallest fixSize
A1Health fields bind to enrollment, not the childRe-bind registry entries to customer_member; migrate field_valuesSmall
D1kind: "document" declared but not authorableA doc_type catalog plus a satisfaction evaluator. The store already existsMedium
B1No child-scoped structured health-fact entity or providerOne entity with fact_kind, one provider definition, one resolver, one new provider kindLarge
C1No document owner outside a form submissionWithdrawn — public.documents is sufficient—

Jurisdiction needs no rules engine. A jurisdiction is a different published Business Process revision — normalizePublishedStageRequirements makes every revision self-contained, so an Oregon org's revision requires Oregon's documents and no other revision knows it exists. Program is applies_to_transition_keys plus field visibility; age group is scope: each_child; industry is carried by nothing at all, because nothing in A–E names a domain.

Needs your decision

  1. 1Billing composition. B as recommended, or A because it is buildable today with zero new truth.
  2. 2A1 migrates live data. Re-binding health fields moves existing field_values rows between entity grains. Reversible, but it touches tenant data.
  3. 3B1 adds a canonical entity and a new provider kind — a platform-vocabulary change, not a feature.
  4. 4Medication authorization is both a document and a requirement. Which one the card shows changes what “Missing” means. I recommend the requirement, with the document as its evidence.
  5. 5Should an “active condition” distinction exist? It would justify a stronger alarm than the restrained treatment now on the card. Absent it, all critical facts are treated as durable safety information.
